sector_model: Building products manufacturer (cyclical, capital intensive): P/E, FCF after capex, gross margin, capacity ramp, channel inventory, leverage.
thesis: Trex (NYSE: TREX), largest US composite decking and railing maker. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-04) read: income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, MD&A gross profit and liquidity, buyback note. Q3 net sales 359.5M vs 285.3M (+26%), 9M 1,120.9M (+10.6%); Q3 NI 52.5M vs 51.8M, 9M NI 175.8M vs 188.1M (-6.6%); Q3 gross margin 36.0% vs 40.5% (depreciation, diesel transport, Arkansas plant labour); 9M SG&A +14.4%. TTM NI 178.07M (190.415-188.113+175.772); TTM OCF 313.85M (358.113-292.627+248.363) less PP&E capex 112.75M (223.592-180.214+69.373) = FCF 201.1M; purchased intangibles excluded (about 6M in 9M). Close 49.83 (2026-11-20) x 99,936,893 shares (2026-10-14 cover) = 4.98B = 28.0x TTM NI, FCF yield 4.0%, 4.9x book 1,010.4M. Capex fell from 180M to 69M in 9M as the Arkansas build finished, lifting FCF. Buybacks 208.6M in 9M (5.2M shares; 100M ASR Feb 2026) vs 9M FCF about 179M, funded partly by revolver: debt 170.0M at 4.9% (133.5M at 2025 year end), cash 3.3M, 526.9M undrawn; covenants met. Receivables 222.9M vs 48.1M (seasonal plus higher sales).
counterthesis: Margin is eroding (gross margin -450bp in Q3) as the new Arkansas plant adds depreciation and labour, so +26% sales produced only +1% NI; 28x TTM earnings is not cheap for 9M NI down 6.6%. Pre-tax margin fell. Capex relief flatters FCF; the company has moved from net cash-like to revolver debt while buying back more than FCF. Q3 sales jump may include channel stocking (receivables up 175M; distributor inventory risk is disclosed). 2024 NI was restated upward in the FY2025 10-K companyfacts (226.4M to 238.4M), cause not read. Aug 2026 new Chief Commercial Officer (8-K 5.02 read). Quote is a 11-20 close, drop of about 5.6% from 52.76 on 11-13.
invalidation: Downgrade if gross margin stays below about 36% after Arkansas ramp, receivables or channel inventory stay elevated into Q4, or leverage rises while buybacks continue. Upgrade needs peers (AZEK is not comparable post-acquisition; check Azek/James Hardie, UFP), through-cycle margins, 11-04 release guidance read, and verified quote origins.
